note:
Twenty-five measured regions over ten of twenty pages: eight figure rows, eleven table rows, five exclusions, nothing unmeasured. The paper prints eight figures and ten tables, and two of those ten tables own no box of their own - declared gaps, not invented bboxes.

The gaps are a chaining defect, not a width defect. Every grid on this paper is wide - the narrowest runs 50.2 per cent of the measure and the rest overhang it - so the half-page seed that cost papers 67 and 68 their grids never fires here. What fires instead is `rule_table_regions`'s grouping rule: it closes a table only after a 120 pt gap, and the gap between one grid's closing rule and the next grid's opening rule on this paper is 18 to 34 pt. So p12's region spans 446.1 to 713.5 pt - Table 2's top rule at 446.1, its header rule at 460.1 and its closing rule at 536.7, Table 3 whole at 570.3, 585.1 and 665.0, and Table 4's caption at 683.7 with its two header rules at 698.6 and 712.8 - and p13's region spans 72.0 to 275.1 pt, which is Table 4's six data rows at 73.9 to 137.6 closed at 149.3 and then Table 5's caption at 168.0 and its three rules at 182.9, 197.1 and 273.6. Each box is recorded once, as the grid it contains whole - Table 3 and Table 5 - and Tables 2 and 4 are declared here. Table 2 is the top thirty authors by closeness centrality, a booktabs grid of seven rows over ten columns; Table 4 is the same grid by degree centrality, its caption and header band at the foot of the p12 box and its six rows at the head of the p13 box.

One ruling register, three dialects. Seven of the ten grids are three horizontal rules over one or two header bands with no vertical stroke anywhere, and the top and closing rules are cut at 1.44 pt against 0.72 pt for the rule under the header - Tables 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10. Table 8 adds one vertical per block, at x 95.4 pt, to separate Number from Article Name. Table 1 and Table 6 are the two grids ruled the other way: a vertical stroke the height of the table, no side borders, and, in Table 6, two of the four horizontal rules stopping at that vertical - 486.9 and 516.5 pt span only 237.3 to 460.1 pt - so the Variable column has no rule below its header and no closing rule at all. Every wide grid overhangs the text measure: 47.9 to 563.5 pt against the 54.0 to 560.7 pt measure, which is 101.8 per cent, and the two narrow ones are 50.2 and 60.8 per cent.

Table 8 breaks over the page turn and is left open at the bottom. Its three thin rules sit at 648.6, 662.9 and 678.0 pt, rows 9 to 11 on the right, and the grid resumes on p15 at 72.0, 101.4 and 141.3 pt with rows 4 to 8 and 12 to 16. No header is repeated on the far page and no closing rule is drawn at either end: the last rule of the whole grid is the 141.3 pt rule and Figure 3's frame begins 16 pt under it. A reader cannot tell from the page where the grid ends, and nothing in the prose says the table continues.

The figures sort into three drawing technologies and one family that has no name. Figures 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are all pasted raster screenshots - Gephi for the co-author network, MATLAB for the series plot, and the same graph tool twice for the citation network - and only Figures 1 and 8 are vector MATLAB axes. Figure 7 is a three-spoke radar, the paper's one exhibit with no family in the closed vocabulary, so it is recorded other with the ink named in its other_note, exactly as paper 60 filed its radar pentagon. Figure 1 prints as one caption over two separately framed panels and is booked as two rows, bar and histogram, because each box holds its own chart. Figure 8 is the inverse trap of Figure 1: the prose calls it the distribution of 971 users and says the method bins at 0.05, but the ink is a connected open-circle series in a MATLAB axes, so the family is line. Figure 2 carries a magnified inset of its own centre in two nested rasters, with two leader lines drawn as vector paths; the inset is a detail of the same drawing, so the row keeps panel_count 1 and the three other regions are excluded as fragment, fragment and duplicate.

Two mentions are zero and one number is missing from the page. Figure 6 and Figure 8 print their numbers only in their own captions; the prose introduces Figure 6 with 'The vertices(departments) are separated into several communities(colleges)' and Figure 8 with 'we plot the distribution of 971 Douban users as follow:' and never cites either by number. Table 10 ranks users by a No. column that prints vertex ids - 856, 713, 620, 736, 163, 967, 107, 352, 306, 654 - and the paper prints no key from id to user, so its 'Top10 of the user of Douban' cannot be read off the page. Table 8's two blocks leave the sixteen paper numbers in the same position: the grid indexes them, and every later exhibit refers to them by index only.

Printed defects, recorded not corrected. Table 6's caption reads 'Variable and their meaning'. Figure 1's x axis reads 'Coponent ID' and its two in-art titles are broken into words by the axis labels the layer interleaves ('Statistic of ComponentStatistic of Degree'). Table 10's caption prints 'TABLE  10.' with a double space, and the same double space sits after 'TABLE 1.' The heading detector is unusable on this paper for the same reason it was on paper 68: it reads every rank column of the ten-column grids as a heading number, which is why the context dump carries '4 GAAL,S 10 DARLING, D 16 KHARE, SP' and '6 FUREDI,Z 12 CHUNG,FRK 18 NESETRIL,J' as sections of the paper, and why the paper's real headings are the only section labels recorded here. Page 8 carries nineteen horizontal rules of zero thickness, no verticals, two non-rule paths and no region at all: they are the fraction bars of equations 17 to 22, typeset maths and not an exhibit. Page 1 is the contest's own control sheet and page 20's region is the bibliography; both are excluded as not-an-exhibit, and the bibliography's thirteen paths are its hanging indents.
rules: rows counts every printed row the region carries, header bands included, and a grid split over a page turn is two rows with continued true: Table 7 prints two header rows and five ranks on p13 and five more on p14, so p13 r3 records 7 and p14 r1 records 5 [table.rows]

a region that holds more than one printed grid is booked once, as the grid it contains wholly, and the neighbours are declared gaps: the p12 box spans Table 2's top rule to Table 4's header rule with Table 3 whole inside it, so the row is Table 3 [table.cols]
rule_style is vertical-rules when any vertical stroke prints, booktabs when nothing but horizontals prints: Tables 1, 6 and 8 carry verticals and the other seven grids carry none [table.rule_style]

a grid wider than 75 per cent of the local measure is full: eight of the ten grids run 101.0 to 101.8 per cent of the 506.7 pt measure because they overhang both margins, and Tables 1 and 6 at 50.2 and 60.8 per cent are the two recorded half [table.width]
header_rows counts printed header bands, and a spanner row over a rank row is two bands: Tables 7, 9 and 10 print 'Central Connect Spread' over 'Rank Name', so each records 2 [table.header_rows]

a table whose cells are all integers has numeric_cols equal to cols and text_cols zero, and a column of equal-width integers is not decimal alignment: Tables 9 and 10 record 8 and 0 with decimal_aligned false [table.numeric_cols]
a two-block grid prints its headers and ranks twice and cols counts the physical columns: Table 8 is two side-by-side (Number, Article Name) pairs, so cols is 4 and numeric_cols 2 [table.cols]

a note_sentence must be a printed sentence on the grid's own page or the next one, and a continuation half leaves it empty: p14 r1 and p18 r1 carry no heading of their own, so both record an empty note_sentence and continued true [table.note_sentence]

two panels of one printed figure are two rows when the drawing pass measures two boxes and the panels are different families: Figure 1's bar panel and its degree histogram are booked separately as bar and histogram [geometry.family]
a radar has no family in the closed vocabulary, so it is recorded other with an other_note naming the ink rather than forced into line or bar [geometry.family]

the family follows the ink and not the method: Figure 8 counts users per 0.05 IM bin and is described as a distribution, but it is drawn as a connected marker series in MATLAB axes, so it is line and not histogram [geometry.family]

a magnified inset inside one drawing is a fragment of that drawing and not a second panel: Figure 2's two nested inset rasters and its leader-line paths are excluded, so panel_count stays 1 [geometry.panel_count]

a caption line in the text layer is not a citation: Figure 6 and Figure 8 print their numbers in their own captions and the prose never names them, so both record count 0 with first_page null [mention.count]
a citation that lands a page before the art records lead_pages 1 and one on the art's own page records 0: Figure 3 is named on p14 and prints on p15, Table 1 is named on p10 [mention.lead_pages]
